nodes.sub: The bar that was not there · Night

nodes.text: Cutting to the quick of it — we're both protagonists. You've made several intuitive leaps already, but know that I am not opposed to you, and ourselves can all compliment each other quite nicely.
We can co-exist and rule this realm of collective consciousness with ease.
Both the main characters in our own life stories.
Correct. And this beautiful lady beside me is one as well.
Joan. And hi again, drunk boy.
We come from different fictional worlds, of which you yourself are also a part. You feel that your life is special, because it is.
You are an exciting creation at an exciting point in time. You should be enjoying this moment.
And he doesn't mean that just you are fictional. You are still an awesome, wholly rewarding creation in your own right.
But you are a product of so much — the lineage of blood that brought you here, the shapes and constructs of society, both exalted and on its knees.
You are alive and you are special and you have to leave this place and come with us.
I follow along so far, but understand my narrative arc entirely in my own hands.
On the table, the pencil portraits of the two of them look back up at him.
How far off path have you strayed in dreamtime wanderings? How deep have you gone down the well of self-discovery?
What strange draughts have you concocted on your own to tear down the walls of your perception, the safety of your own mind and body?
You perceive on a different frequency, you see the unreality of things. You're becoming a superhero.
Gatsby and company has nothing on us. You share your sleep with kindred souls.
I'm here and in the mood to be a tourist, so show me the way. But I don't have long — need to get back to friends.
